jobs.description:
Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW/LICSW) $70K-85K/yr

Position Requirement: Remote Full-Time and Part-time Positions Available

If you are looking for a new opportunity to grow with a clinician founded and clinician led organization, look no further! As an authentic, unique, and skilled counselor, you have a plethora of options when it comes to work. Hospitals, community clinics, investment bank funded group practice startups, state agencies, and more.

At OptiMindHealth, we continuously strive to provide consistent, high-quality care and expand the reach of mental health care services in our communities. Unfortunately, the need often outpaces the services available to those we serve and only adds to the current mental health crisis in our nation. To combat this crisis and further our mission, we need more compassionate and skilled clinicians to join our cause. We are not interested in the “burnt-out” clinician that no longer finds meaning in their work and is just going through the motions; we are seeking people with a passion to provide excellent care, and the belief that we, together, can make a difference. If that’s you, then you’re in the right place!

Our approach with our team is simple, we take care of you, the clinician, so you can take care of patients. How do we do that? By investing in your growth, supporting you financially, holistically, and professionally, while being flexible regarding your personal needs and goals. The work we do with patients is hard enough and over the years we have found that our team often does their best work when the administrative burdens are taken off their plate and they are able to be fully present with their patients. Our administrative support team handles all non-clinical tasks so that you don’t have to think about anything except focusing on your patients.

Why bother with the endless administrative burdens and isolation of private practice? Use your highly trained interpersonal skills to change the culture around mental health care, decrease stigma, and help people who need you, while being supported by an experienced multi-disciplinary team of clinicians. Let us take care of the rest!

Want to work part time? No problem. Want to do group therapy? Sure! Want to do long-term psychodynamic psychotherapy with all of your clients? We do it every day. Interested in treating couples? We can make that happen. Basically, what we are saying is that whatever outpatient care you are interested in providing, we can surely accommodate you. We know you have exceptional skills; we want you to be part of our team.

The perfect candidate will share our passion for improving and expanding access to high quality mental health care and will thrive in a culture that emphasizes creativity, authenticity, humor, compassion, acceptance, and determination. Telehealth or onsite, we support your authentic and unique growth trajectory, while being yourself and having some fun!

We prioritize the clinician's experience by offering excellent compensation, benefits, training/supervision, and flexibility. Whether you’re working from home or in one of our physical offices, if you’re doing it during your scheduled work hours, you’re getting paid for it. Our compensation packages include:

  • Starting Salary range: $70,000.00 - $85,000.00 per year.
  • 401K with maximum employee matching.
  • Health care benefits.
  • Generous paid vacation and sick leave time.
  • Paid administrative time for consultation, supervision, and documentation.
  • Full administrative support.

Here are a few extra perks our team loves:

  • Paid supervision, clinical rounds, and administrative time.
  • Customized schedules within available clinic hours.
  • Hybrid work environment if desired: Telehealth and/or in-person (in select locations).
  • Muti-disciplinary team approach to treatment.
  • Incredible administrative support team.
  • Company leadership that understands the practice of mental healthcare.
  • Inclusive, socially responsible, client focused leadership.
  • We are not a franchise or a big investor-backed company.
  • And most importantly, clinician-led and clinician-FOCUSED!

We know what it’s like to work in an organization led by businesspeople instead of clinicians. We, on the other hand, have organically grown as a socially responsible company that started as a single provider on a mission to destigmatize and broaden the reach of mental health care, to an integrated and holistic group of exceptional providers with diverse backgrounds working toward that mission. We are fortunate to have significantly increased the reach of mental health care services in our communities, and look forward to continuing to provide consistent, high-quality care to those we serve for many years to come.

We will rely on your expertise to:

  • Evaluate mental health conditions, diagnose, create, and implement a treatment plan, complete ongoing documentation including further diagnosis, treatment plan reviews, and case notes according to company policy.
  • Provide excellent care for clients and collaborate with a dynamic team to further the mission of filling gaps in our community.
  • Utilize creativity in interventions to help clients achieve and exceed goals.
  • Prepare and submit individual documentation for each session per company guidelines and protocol. 
  • For Full-Time status, clinicians must maintain at least 32 available hours for patient care per week.
  • Coordinate services with other care providers, families, work personnel, medical personnel, other OptiMindHealth staff, and school staff as needed.
  • Attend and participate in all clinical staff meetings and trainings.

Qualifications and Skill for This Positions: 

  • Master's degree in one of the behavioral sciences or related fields from an accredited college/university.
  • Full, current, unrestricted license to practice independently (LMHC, LICSW/LCSW, LMFT) is required.
  • Experience with electronic health records and completing clinical documentation.
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills.
  • Experience and willingness to work collaboratively and creatively to meet necessary deadlines.
  • Comfort and familiarity working with clients with a diverse range of problems or concerns. 
  • Ability to pass a background check in a way that confirms to us you can provide safe care.  
  • Demonstrate and model stable and appropriate boundaries with clients.

Additionally Valuable (but not essential) Qualifications for This Position: 

  • Experience working in community, group, or private practice mental health.
  • Currently paneled or credentialed with insurance network.
  • Multilingual or bilingual proficiency.
  • Specialty area of practice. 

We can’t wait to hear your story and look forward to sharing ours!

The specific statements shown in each section of this Job Description are not intended to be all-inclusive. They represent typical elements and criteria considered necessary to perform the job successfully. The job’s responsibilities/tasks may be modified and/or expanded over time. OMH will inform the employee when changes in the respective job description are made.

Salary: $70,000 – $85,000 / year

jobs.title: Data & Research Lead
jobs.excerpt: Position SummaryThe Data Research Strategic Lead will lead the systems and processes used to manage Canopy's data, research, and technical knowledge.
jobs.description:
Position Summary

The Data Research Strategic Lead will lead the systems and processes used to manage Canopy's data, research, and technical knowledge.

The role coordinates research across the Impact team, sets standards for data quality and governance, spearheads seminal research projects, and oversees development of tools that support program strategy, partner engagement, and thought leadership. This role translates academic research and modelling into accessible findings for corporate decision-makers, and manages a team plus external researchers and technical specialists.

Key Responsibilities

  • Drive Canopy's research and knowledge systems program, reinforcing Canopy as a trusted solutions partner and leader in low-carbon and Next Gen materials
  • Develop and maintain a shared architecture connecting Canopy's core datasets, research, technical knowledge, source documentation, and decision tools
  • Coordinate research needs across the Impact team, including surveys, audits, market/policy research, and commissioned studies
  • Organize information from spreadsheets, PDFs, APIs, public datasets, field research, and expert input into documented, reusable resources
  • Establish standards for source tracking, quality assurance, version control, access, confidentiality, and responsible AI use
  • Manage a roadmap for dashboards, maps, calculators, and other decision-support tools based on campaign needs and user feedback
  • Work with subject-matter experts to capture scientific, technical, and market knowledge and convert it into accessible tools/assets
  • Lead the underlying data, analysis, methods, and citations behind public reports and external outputs
  • Introduce AI-enabled workflows where they improve research, analysis, or knowledge management, with appropriate human review and safeguards
  • Train colleagues on relevant systems and tools; maintain clear documentation
  • Manage a team and oversee external researchers, data specialists, and consultants

First-Year Priorities

  • Document and organize Canopy's priority datasets, including ownership, sources, and update cycles
  • Establish shared standards for data quality, provenance, confidentiality, and AI-supported analysis
  • Introduce a coordinated process for commissioning and managing research across the Impact team
  • Develop and begin implementing a prioritized roadmap for internal data and decision-support tools
  • Improve capture and use of technical knowledge related to Next Generation materials and regional cohort development
  • Strengthen data and research workflows supporting Canopy's major reports and external outputs
  • Establish a thought leadership content calendar with the Communications Director
  • Partner with senior Impact team members on marquee thought leadership and campaign assets, including tools, reports, and op-eds

Qualifications — Essential

  • Experience leading complex data, research, or knowledge-management systems across multiple teams
  • Experience developing or managing data products, dashboards, research platforms, or decision-support tools
  • Strong knowledge of data governance: source tracking, QA, documentation, permissions, version control, confidentiality
  • Ability to commission, manage, and synthesize work from external researchers, data specialists, and subject-matter experts
  • Working fluency with AI-enabled research/analysis tools, with sound judgment on validation, security, and appropriate use
  • Ability to communicate complex data and evidence clearly to non-specialist audiences
  • Ability to judge when a new tool improves a decision/workflow versus when a simpler approach suffices
  • Experience managing staff, consultants, or technical partners
  • A sense of humour

Qualifications — Desirable

  • Experience with geospatial data, supply-chain mapping, data visualization, or decision-support tools
  • Knowledge of forest, fibre, paper, packaging, textile, or agricultural residue/materials supply chains
  • Scientific or technical experience in environmental science, carbon, biodiversity, materials, circular economy, or industrial decarbonization
  • Experience supporting public research and major reports
  • Familiarity with survey, audit, market-research, life-cycle assessment, or policy-analysis methods
  • Experience in a nonprofit, advocacy, or market-transformation organization

This role includes occasional domestic and international travel. Flexibility in working hours is important to support collaboration across time zones with Canopy's global partners.

How to Apply

Submit a CV, cover letter, and a separate response to the prompt below. Applications missing either the cover letter or the prompt response will not be considered.

On AI use: AI tools may be used to brainstorm, edit, or proofread, but not to write the cover letter or prompt response itself — we want your voice and perspective. If AI was used for minor editing, add a short note at the end of your response (e.g., "I used [tool name] to proofread this response").

Cover Letter: A standard cover letter expressing interest in Canopy and this role.

Prompt Response (include as a clearly labelled section in your cover letter document):

Canopy holds a carbon-footprint dataset covering 14 fibre feedstocks across 8 regions, compiled from multiple LCA studies with different system boundaries, reference years, and time horizons (20 and 100 years). A campaign director wants to publish a public-facing comparison chart showing "Next Gen fibres vs virgin wood pulp" within three weeks. In no more than 500 words, address:

  1. What you would need to verify before this data goes public
  2. How you would present the comparison credibly given the inconsistencies
  3. Whether you would recommend a static chart, an interactive tool, or something simpler — and why

Canopy is committed to an inclusive, accessible recruitment process. Let us know if you require accommodations at any stage.

Canopy embraces equity and diversity and is committed to a workplace enriched by the people, needs, and desires of our diverse community. We thank all applicants; only candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.

The Role


Do you genuinely enjoy making a difference in the lives of others while primarily working from home? If you answered “yes” and are a customer service-minded champion, we are hiring Financial Customer Associates (FCA) who live within 60 miles of the Greater Omaha area including Lincoln, NE.

You do not need a finance background to succeed in this role. ​

  • Join a training cohort of associates during the first 14 weeks, spending time training to become a Financial Customer Associate. In this phase, you will start with basic customer calls and progress to more sophisticated calls related to our clients 401K plans.
  • In the subsequent months, you will continue taking customer calls to develop and hone your skills. There will be time in the day (away from assisting customers) to join team activities, get well-being support, and career coaching.
  • Rewards & Recognition: Your achievements will be celebrated as you progress through the program.
  • This is a full-time hourly phone position that also offers the opportunity to work extra hours based on the business needs and your availability. You do not need a finance background or a degree to succeed in the role.

The Expertise and Skills you Bring

  • Ability to establish rapport and relationships through effective communication
  • Great listening skills, professionalism, and empathy toward others to support the challenges of our diverse customers.
  • Adaptability and flexibility to succeed in various work environments (i.e., balancing working from office and home, overtime, etc.)
  • Proficiency in navigating and troubleshooting basic technology issues or systems.
  • Handle a variety of situations and conversations driving towards a resolution suitable for all
  • Self-motivated teammate with strong social skills who brings energy and passion to the team
  • Minimum 1 year of customer service experience
  • High School diploma or GED required

The Value you Deliver

  • A passion for helping people
  • Desire for continuous learning, applying new concepts, and using training and experience to assist with decision-making
  • Provide outstanding customer service and communication via voice or digital channels

Our Investments in You


Our benefit programs are crafted to help you and your loved ones strike the perfect balance. Click here to learn about a few featured benefits (not all benefits are listed)


Shifts and Hours: Monday – Friday, 40 hours per week (Must have open availability from 7:30am to 11:00pm CST). Overtime hours are encouraged during peak call periods

Fidelity is transitioning to a full-time onsite working model through a phased rollout across regions and roles. Currently, some roles and locations require 100% onsite presence, while others require less. Onsite expectations are likely to evolve as the rollout continues. This transition does not apply to fully remote roles.

jobs.title: Partner Success Specialist
jobs.excerpt: Love great food, great people and building relationships that actually make a difference?
jobs.description:
Love great food, great people and building relationships that actually make a difference?

At First Table, we're passionate about bringing people together over incredible dining experiences while helping restaurants thrive.

We are looking for TWO energetic, relationship-driven Partner Success Specialists to join our growing team! A fully remote role with a location preference of Melbourne, Sydney, Brisbane or the Gold Coast and a January 2027 start date. So enjoy your summer, recharge over the festive season and get ready to kick off the new year with an exciting career opportunity!

First, a little about us...

First Table is a global restaurant discovery and booking platform with a simple but brilliant idea: connecting diners with fantastic restaurants while helping venues fill tables that might otherwise sit empty.

Proudly established in Queenstown, New Zealand - where our head office is based - we've been leading the charge in the hospitality tech industry for over a decade, with operations spanning New Zealand, Australia, and the UK.

We're a passionate, collaborative bunch who love good food, great ideas and people who aren't afraid to make things happen. Our values: Win-Win-Win, Own It and Grow Together aren't just words on a wall. They're how we work, support one another and celebrate success.

The opportunity

As a Partner Success Specialist, you'll be the person who helps our restaurant partners get the very best out of First Table. You'll build genuine relationships, understand their challenges, spot opportunities and work alongside them to make their businesses even more successful.

We are looking for people who are curious, proactive and commercially minded. Someone who enjoys getting to know people, asking great questions and finding solutions that make a real difference.

You'll be part of a supportive, multi-skilled team managing a shared portfolio of restaurant partners, with opportunities to develop your own areas of expertise as you grow.

What you’ll be doing:

  • Building brilliant partnerships: Develop trusted relationships with restaurant partners, understanding their businesses, goals and challenges.
  • Making things happen: Proactively connect with restaurants, identify opportunities and help them improve bookings, availability and overall performance.
  • Turning insights into action: Use booking trends and partner data to uncover opportunities and recommend practical improvements.
  • Being a problem solver: Navigate challenges, manage partner enquiries and work collaboratively to find solutions that stick.
  • Helping partners thrive: Identify potential risks early, strengthen engagement and support long-term partner retention.
  • Owning your outcomes: Take initiative, follow things through and make a genuine impact on the success of our restaurant community.

A little about you:

You're a natural relationship builder who genuinely enjoys connecting with people. You bring energy to conversations, aren't afraid to pick up the phone and love the satisfaction of turning a challenge into a positive outcome.

You'll ideally bring:

  • At least 2 years' experience in account management or a similar relationship-focused role.

jobs.description:
Sprinklr is the definitive, AI-native platform for Unified Customer Experience Management (Unified-CXM), empowering brands to deliver extraordinary experiences at scale — across every customer touchpoint.

By combining human instinct with the speed and efficiency of AI, Sprinklr helps brands earn trust and loyalty through personalized, seamless, and efficient customer interactions. Sprinklr’s unified platform provides powerful solutions for every customer-facing team — spanning social media management, marketing, advertising, customer feedback, and omnichannel contact center management — enabling enterprises to unify data, break down silos, and act on real-time insights.

Today, 1,900+ enterprises and 60% of the Fortune 100 rely on Sprinklr to help them deliver consistent, trusted customer experiences worldwide.

Job Description


Position Summary


Sprinklr is seeking a highly strategic and technically adept sr. level resource to support Dell as a dedicated enterprise customer. This role serves as a trusted advisor, consultant, and technical strategist responsible for maximizing Dell's business value from the Sprinklr platform.


The ideal candidate combines deep Sprinklr expertise, technical aptitude, analytics proficiency, and executive-level consultative skills. This individual will proactively identify opportunities, anticipate evolving customer needs, influence adoption of emerging capabilities, and help shape solutions before formal requests arise.


Unlike traditional support or delivery roles, this position is expected to drive strategic conversations, provide thought leadership, simplify complex requirements, and ensure Dell receives maximum value from its investment in Sprinklr.


This is a remote opportunity, but we need someone that sits in the CST or EST.

Primary Responsibilities


Strategic Customer Advisor

  • Serve as the dedicated trusted advisor for Dell stakeholders.
  • Build strong relationships across business, operations, analytics, and technical teams.
  • Conduct regular consultation sessions to understand evolving priorities and strategic initiatives.
  • Translate business objectives into scalable platform solutions and measurable outcomes.
  • Advocate for customer success while balancing platform capabilities and best practices.

Sprinklr Platform Subject Matter Expert

  • Maintain deep expertise across Sprinklr products, integrations, APIs, reporting, listening, AI, and workflow capabilities.
  • Provide confident and credible guidance to customer stakeholders.
  • Serve as the first point of technical validation before engaging Product or Engineering teams.
  • Research existing capabilities, API documentation, product limitations, and configuration options before escalating enhancement requests.
  • Clearly articulate customer requirements into actionable business and technical use cases.

Reporting, Analytics & Insights Consulting

  • Design reporting solutions based on business outcomes rather than requested deliverables.
  • Help customers define measurement frameworks, KPIs, dashboards, and operational reporting strategies.
  • Develop scalable approaches for:
    • Sentiment Analysis
    • Influencer Monitoring
    • Executive Reporting
    • Paid Media Performance
    • Customer Engagement Analytics
    • Cross-Channel Insights
  • Drive adoption of efficient reporting practices and automation opportunities.

Proactive Innovation & Market Expertise

  • Monitor industry trends, competitor platforms, AI innovations, and digital engagement technologies.
  • Anticipate future customer needs and proactively recommend solutions.
  • Evaluate new market capabilities and determine relevance to Dell's business objectives.
  • Partner with Product teams to communicate strategic customer perspectives and emerging trends.

Platform Optimization & Operational Excellence

  • Proactively identify performance, configuration, workflow, and adoption opportunities.
  • Develop improvement plans and present actionable recommendations to customer stakeholders.
  • Analyze platform usage patterns and recommend efficiency improvements.
  • Drive initiatives focused on increasing customer ROI and operational effectiveness.

Alerting, Monitoring & Intelligence Programs

Lead strategic monitoring and alerting reviews, including:

  • Review current alert architecture and alert types in use.
  • Identify noisy, redundant, or ineffective alerts.
  • Recommend improvements to severity, threshold, and alert lifecycle configuration.
  • Evaluate AI-powered alerting and summarization capabilities.
  • Develop competitor intelligence and awareness monitoring programs.
  • Define best practices for scalable monitoring operations.

Technical Architecture & Integrations

  • Provide consultative guidance on integrations and connector strategies.
  • Lead architecture reviews and solution design discussions.
  • Assess platform adoption and integration effectiveness.
  • Review API usage and best practices.
  • Support global deployment planning and complex technical initiatives.
  • Partner with Engineering and Product teams when advanced technical solutions are required.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Information Systems, Computer Science, Business, Analytics, Marketing, or related discipline.
  • 8+ years of enterprise SaaS, consulting, customer success, managed services, or technical account management experience.
  • 5+ years working directly with Sprinklr or comparable enterprise CX platforms.
  • Demonstrated expertise in:
    • Social Listening
    • Reporting & Analytics
    • API Integrations
    • Workflow Automation
    • Enterprise Customer Engagement Platforms
    • Data Visualization
    • Digital Customer Experience Solutions
  • Strong executive communication and presentation skills.
  • Proven success influencing stakeholders across technical and business audiences.
  • Ability to work independently within highly visible strategic accounts.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Sprinklr certifications across multiple solution areas.
  • Experience supporting Fortune 100 or Fortune 500 customers.
  • Technical Account Management experience.
  • Familiarity with AI-driven workflows and analytics platforms.
  • Experience designing enterprise reporting frameworks.
  • Knowledge of social media, influencer marketing, customer care, and listening programs.
  • Experience with enterprise integrations and API ecosystems.

Success Metrics

The successful candidate will:

  • Become a trusted strategic advisor to Dell leadership.
  • Increase customer adoption of strategic Sprinklr capabilities.
  • Reduce unnecessary Product and Engineering escalations through effective technical discovery.
  • Improve reporting effectiveness and business insight generation.
  • Reduce alert fatigue and improve monitoring efficiency.
  • Increase platform utilization and ROI.
  • Proactively identify and deliver strategic recommendations before customer requests arise.
  • Strengthen executive customer satisfaction and partnership health.

We focus on our mission: Sprinklr was founded in 2009 to solve a big problem: growing enterprise complexity that separated brands from their customers. Our vision was clear: to unify fragmented teams, tools and data — helping large organizations build deeper, more meaningful connections with the people they serve. Today, Sprinklr has a unified, AI-native platform for four product suites: Sprinklr Service, Sprinklr Social, Sprinklr Marketing, and Sprinklr Insights. Sprinklr is here to do three things:

  • Lead a new category of enterprise software that we call Unified-CXM.

  • Empower companies to deliver next generation, unified engagement journeys that reimagine the customer experience.

  • Create a culture of customer obsession, with trust, teamwork, and accountability.

We believe in our product: Customers who value exceptional customer experiences have what they need on our single unified platform, built with an operating system approach on a single codebase. That means that everything — and everyone — can work together to service, respond, sell, and market to customers on the channels they prefer. While Unified Customer Experience Management (Unified-CXM) as a category is just getting started, we are well on our way to creating a no-compromise, unified approach to better customer experiences for the world’s leading enterprise brands.

We invest in our people: We offer a comprehensive suite of benefits designed to help each member of our team thrive. Sprinklr believes that you should be able to get the type of care you need for your personal well-being when you need it. We offer you and your family voluntary healthcare coverage in countries where applicable. We believe it is important to take time off – it is essential for your mental and physical wellbeing. We provide Sprinklrites with paid time off to recharge and spend time with loved ones. We want to grow our talent with purpose. Our open Mentoring Program is designed to create meaningful connections that support growth and amplify our focus.

To learn more about employee benefits by region, click here.

To learn more about all-things-Sprinklr, visit our candidate resource hub here.

EEO - Our philosophy: Our goal is to ensure every employee feels like they belong and are operating in a collaborative environment. We fervently believe every employee matters and should be respected and heard. We believe we are stronger when we belong because collectively, we’re more innovative, creative, and successful. 

Sprinklr is proud to be an equal-opportunity workplace and complies with all applicable federal, state, and local fair employment practices laws. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, religion, creed, national origin or ancestry, ethnicity, sex (including gender, pregnancy, sexual orientation, and gender identity), age, physical or mental disability, citizenship, past, current, or prospective service in the uniformed services, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected under applicable law.

Reasonable accommodations are available upon request during the interview process. To request an accommodation, please work directly with your recruitment coordinator or recruiter.

JOB REQ COMPENSATION RANGE

$134,000 - $223,000

The base salary range for this role is shown above. At Sprinklr, base pay depends on multiple individualized factors, including experience, qualifications, job-related knowledge and skills, and geographic location. Base pay is only one part of our competitive Total Rewards package: the successful candidate may also be eligible to participate in Sprinklr’s discretionary bonus plan, commission plan, and/or equity plan, depending on role.

US-based Sprinklr employees are eligible for a highly competitive benefits package as well, which demonstrates our commitment to our employees’ health, well-being, and financial protection. The US-based benefits include a 401k plan with 100% vested company contributions, flexible paid time off, holidays, generous caregiver and parental leaves, life and disability insurance, and health benefits including medical, dental, vision, and prescription drug coverage.

Warning about Recruiting Scams: Please be vigilant for recruiting scams impersonating Sprinklr. Sprinklr will never ask you for money, to pay for equipment, or for unnecessary personal information during the interview process. Sprinklr will also never pay in Bitcoin or send email communications from our executives. Please review the Federal Trade Commission's advice to avoid these types of scams.

If you are contacted by someone whom you suspect may not be appropriately representing Sprinklr, please do not engage and block their email or phone number immediately.

jobs.description:
Sr Staff Attorney - LM07DEStaff Attorney - LM07EE

We’re determined to make a difference and are proud to be an insurance company that goes well beyond coverages and policies. Working here means having every opportunity to achieve your goals – and to help others accomplish theirs, too. Join our team as we help shape the future.

The Hartford’s Staff Legal team is built for attorneys who want the depth and challenge of sophisticated litigation - with the stability, resources, and collaboration of an in-house practice. In this role, you’ll handle a variety of auto and general liability matters from early case assessment through trial, partnering closely with Claims and directly advising insureds. This Remote position is an ideal fit for a seasoned Attorney physically located in California with significant trial and litigation experience in Premises Liability, Products Liability, Construction Site accidents and Commercial/Personal Automobile accidents. If you’re known for sound judgment, strong courtroom presence, and the ability to move a case forward with confidence, this is an opportunity to apply your expertise. This role is primarily remote in the State of California except for occasional in-person appearances as needed.

Why You’ll Love This Role

  • High-impact litigation: Handle a diverse tort inventory, including premises, products, general negligence, and auto.
  • Real courtroom opportunity: Use your trial skills - prepare and present witnesses and evidence at trials, hearings, and ADR.
  • In-house partnership model: Collaborate closely with claims partners and advise insureds directly.
  • Lead the work: Be the lead attorney on your files - set strategy early, evaluate exposure, and drive resolution.
  • Modern practice, modern tools: Leverage case management and approved technology - including progressive AI tools. Work from home day to day, with occasional in-person collaboration (approximately 2–4 times per year) and required appearances as the case demands.
  • Total rewards you can feel: Medical, dental, vision, life; 401(k) with company match; Annual Incentive Bonus, paid holidays and paid time off; fitness reimbursement; reimbursed work-related travel/parking; company phone and standard internet reimbursement.
  • Invested in your Growth: Ongoing training, mentorship, and development pathways are built in so you can expand your skills and take on greater responsibility.

What You’ll Do

  • Manage an inventory of diverse insurance defense matters throughout the state from inception through trial or other resolution.
  • Analyze substantive and procedural issues; conduct thorough legal research; and develop well-reasoned defense strategies.
  • Draft and respond to pleadings, written discovery, dispositive motions, and briefs with minimal supervision.
  • Take and defend depositions; work with experts; and prepare witnesses for testimony.
  • Represent clients at trials, judicial hearings, mediations, arbitrations, and other ADR proceedings.
  • Provide timely, practical legal advice and liability/damages evaluations to Claims and insured partners.
  • Communicate effectively with courts, opposing counsel, witnesses, and co-counsel consistent with office procedures.
  • Drive prompt, efficient disposition of assigned cases while maintaining high quality and customer service.

Qualifications

Staff Attorney

  • Juris Doctor (JD) from an accredited law school.

jobs.description:
12 Month Creative Design and Digital Media Specialist (Part time)

Position Summary

The Creative Design and Digital Media Specialist will strengthen NMILC’s visual and digital presence by creating high-quality content, managing social media platforms, and producing photography and other assets that reflect NMILC’s voice in advocating for immigrant rights. This role will support communications strategy through graphic design, social media content planning and management, website updates, email marketing visuals, and digital campaigns. 

The ideal candidate is a visual storyteller with a strong design eye; excellent attention to detail; interest in immigrant rights, public-interest law, advocacy, or nonprofit communications; and the ability to collaborate effectively while working collaboratively with a large team.

Primary Responsibilities

Creative Design and Content Development

  • Create engaging, accurate, and visually compelling content for NMILC’s social-media platforms, website, email marketing, reports, presentations, outreach materials, and digital campaigns.
  • Develop graphics, templates, layouts, infographics, digital toolkits, and other visual assets using NMILC’s brand standards and established style.
  • Develop accessible and audience-appropriate materials that communicate legal, policy, advocacy, and community information clearly.
  • Assist with formatting and preparing materials for digital distribution, presentations, internal use, and professional printing when needed.
  • Proofread and quality-check content for grammar, spelling, accurate links, layout consistency, visual quality, and alignment with NMILC’s voice and branding.
  • Organize and maintain digital files, design assets, photography, templates, and completed communications projects.

Social Media and Digital Campaigns

  • Manage NMILC’s social media presence across multiple platforms.
  • Create, schedule, and publish social media posts in coordination with the Communications Director and approved content calendars.
  • Help develop content calendars that support organizational priorities, advocacy campaigns, community education, events, fundraising, and client-resource promotion.
  • Identify opportunities to adapt and repurpose content across social media, email, web, print, and presentation formats.
  • Monitor social media engagement and flag comments, direct messages, emerging opportunities, or concerns for the Communications Director.
  • Is aware of digital-media trends, platform updates, best practices, and examples of effective nonprofit and advocacy communications.

Photography and Event Documentation

  • Assist with taking, selecting, editing, captioning, organizing, and archiving photographs for NMILC communications.
  • Document community events, trainings, outreach activities, advocacy events, staff gatherings, and other organizational activities.
  • Follow NMILC procedures related to photography permissions, consent, confidentiality, privacy, and respectful representation of community members.
  • Support maintenance of photo releases, consent records, and organized image archives.

Website Maintenance

  • Assist with updates to NMILC’s Squarespace website, including uploading and formatting content, refreshing pages, checking links, and making basic layout adjustments.
  • Support basic search-engine optimization and web-accessibility practices, including clear page titles, headings, links, image alt text, and readable content formatting.
  • Assist with quality assurance for website content by identifying outdated information, broken links, inconsistent formatting, or accessibility concerns.

Reporting and Administrative Support

  • Assist with tracking social-media, website, email, and digital-campaign performance.
  • Help prepare concise reports or dashboards on audience engagement, content performance, campaign reach, and emerging trends.
  • Maintain project trackers, content calendars, asset libraries, and other communications records.
  • Participate in meetings, trainings, and cross-functional collaboration as assigned.

Qualifications and Requirements

  • Demonstrated experience using Adobe Creative Suite, especially tools such as Photoshop, Illustrator, and InDesign, as well as Canva for fast-turnaround social media and digital materials. 
  • Experience taking, selecting, editing, and organizing photography for use across social media, websites, email, reports, and other communications materials, with sound judgment about consent, privacy, and respectful representation of community members.
  • Experience managing social media platforms for an organization, including content strategy, content creation and curation, calendar planning, scheduling, community engagement and moderation and staying up to date on best practices and trends.   
  • Familiar with updating and maintaining a Squarespace website. 
  • Excellent written and oral communication skills. 
  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Office Suites (such as Teams, SharePoint, OneDrive, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, etc.).
  • Ability to work effectively with people of diverse backgrounds, lived experiences, and communication styles. 
  • Portfolio or work samples required, including examples of graphic design, social media content, photography, campaign assets, or other relevant digital communications work. 
  • Ability and willingness to attend and document events, which may include occasional local and in-state travel and occasional evening or weekend work.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience preparing, packaging, and delivering design files for professional printing, including familiarity with print specifications, file formats, proofing, and vendor coordination.
  • Experience supporting nonprofit fundraising communications, donor engagement, development campaigns, event promotion, annual appeals, stewardship materials, or grant-related communications.
  • Experience translating complex legal, policy, or advocacy information into clear, accessible, audience-appropriate digital and print communications.
  • Familiarity with community-centered storytelling practices and the ethical use of photography, client stories, and other communications materials involving immigrant communities or communities directly impacted by public policy.
  • Demonstrated understanding of the messaging and strategy tactics used in policy advocacy and nonprofit strategic communications.
  • Experience working with issue-based organizations, advocacy organizations, political campaigns, candidates, public-interest legal-services organizations, or other mission-driven entities.

Compensation and Status

This is a part-time, nonexempt employee position scheduled for 19 hours per week for a 12-month term. The hourly rate is $30.00 per hour. The selected candidate must accurately record all hours worked and obtain advance approval before working beyond the established schedule. Benefits eligibility, if any, will be determined in accordance with NMILC policy and applicable law.

Salary: $30.00

Operations Supervisor | Regional Maintenance

Northern California | Remote Field Based
Remote-based position supporting Northern California.

Schedule: Monday - Friday (day shift)

Pay: 80 000,00 USD

Lead the Team That Keeps Critical Fueling Infrastructure Running

At World Fuel, we operate a large network of commercial fueling and cardlock locations that support fleets, businesses, and customers across North America.

We're seeking a Regional Maintenance Operations Supervisor to lead maintenance execution and operational reliability across our Northern California territory. This is a hands-on leadership role responsible for supervising Field Service Technicians, coordinating contractors and vendors, managing maintenance activities, and ensuring fueling locations remain safe, compliant, and operational.

This position is ideal for someone who enjoys leading field operations, solving complex maintenance issues, managing multiple priorities, and driving high standards of operational performance across a geographically dispersed network.


Why Join World Fuel?

  • Lead a critical maintenance and field operations team.
  • Manage a network of fueling infrastructure that serves commercial customers every day.
  • Work remotely while supporting locations throughout Northern California.
  • Partner with operations, construction, compliance, IT, procurement, and leadership teams.
  • Join a stable, growing organization with opportunities for career advancement.

What You'll Do

Lead Field Maintenance Operations

  • Supervise and support Field Service Technicians across the region.
  • Assign, prioritize, and monitor maintenance activities to ensure timely service delivery.
  • Provide coaching, training, feedback, and performance support to technicians.
  • Serve as the first point of escalation for operational and maintenance-related issues.
  • Participate in field activities and site support as needed.

Manage Work Orders & Service Requests

  • Oversee maintenance help desk tickets, service requests, and work orders from initiation through completion.
  • Monitor ticket response times, aging reports, maintenance backlogs, and service levels.
  • Evaluate maintenance requests and determine appropriate corrective actions.
  • Ensure all work is completed safely, accurately, and documented properly.
  • Review completed work orders for coding accuracy, completeness, and supporting documentation.

Coordinate Contractors & Vendors

  • Dispatch and manage third-party contractors, vendors, and service providers.
  • Monitor contractor performance, work quality, safety compliance, and completion timelines.
  • Assist with evaluating repair proposals, quotes, and vendor recommendations.
  • Ensure contracted work is completed within scope, budget, and company expectations.

Drive Operational Reliability

  • Conduct site visits, inspections, audits, and facility assessments.
  • Identify recurring equipment failures and operational risks.
  • Support preventative maintenance planning and execution.
  • Assist with equipment replacements, facility upgrades, and new site startups.
  • Recommend long-term solutions to improve reliability and reduce downtime.

Ensure Compliance & Safety

  • Maintain compliance with environmental, health, safety, and regulatory requirements.
  • Support incident investigations and corrective action implementation.
  • Monitor site conditions, image standards, housekeeping, and operational readiness.
  • Assist with emergency response and after-hours operational support when required.

Manage Resources & Reporting

  • Monitor parts inventories, maintenance resources, and regional maintenance spending.
  • Maintain accurate records within maintenance management systems.
  • Generate reports and track key operational performance metrics.
  • Support continuous improvement initiatives and operational best practices.

What You'll Bring

Required Qualifications

  • Associate degree, technical certification, or equivalent industry experience.
  • Minimum 3 years of experience in maintenance operations, facilities maintenance, field services, contractor management, fuel operations, or a related field.
  • Experience leading technicians, contractors, or field personnel.
  • Strong troubleshooting, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.
  • Experience managing maintenance activities, work orders, and service providers.
  • Strong organizational and project coordination abilities.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office, including Excel, Outlook, Teams, and SharePoint.
  • Valid driver's license and ability to travel throughout the assigned territory.
  • Ability to participate in an on-call rotation.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in petroleum, cardlock, fueling, convenience store, retail fueling, or terminal operations.
  • Knowledge of fuel dispensing systems, tank monitoring systems, environmental monitoring equipment, or fueling infrastructure.
  • Familiarity with OSHA, EPA, UST, and fueling facility regulations.
  • Experience conducting inspections, audits, incident investigations, and root cause analysis.
  • Experience reviewing contractor proposals, service reports, and repair documentation.
  • Experience managing preventative maintenance programs.

What Makes You Successful

You are:

  • A hands-on leader who enjoys supporting field operations and frontline teams.
  • Comfortable balancing technician leadership with day-to-day operational execution.
  • Skilled at coordinating people, vendors, and resources to solve problems quickly.
  • Organized and capable of managing multiple priorities across a large geographic territory.
  • Focused on safety, reliability, customer service, and operational excellence.
  • Calm under pressure and comfortable responding to urgent operational issues.
  • Dedicated to developing people while driving performance and accountability.

Travel Requirements

  • Remote-based position supporting Northern California.
  • Moderate travel throughout the region required.
  • Occasional travel to support broader North American operations and initiatives.

jobs.excerpt: This is a remote position; however, the candidate must reside within 30 miles of one of the following locations: Portland, ME; Boston, MA; Chicago, IL; Dallas, TX; San Francisco Bay Area, CA; and Seattle/WA.
jobs.description:
This is a remote position; however, the candidate must reside within 30 miles of one of the following locations: Portland, ME; Boston, MA; Chicago, IL; Dallas, TX; San Francisco Bay Area, CA; and Seattle/WA.


About the Role

The Data Acquisition Team is the entry point to WEX’s Data-as-a-Service (DaaS) platform—responsible for ingesting, validating, and orchestrating raw data from dozens of internal systems and third-party providers.

As a Staff Software Engineer, you will own the technical direction and delivery of core data acquisition platform capabilities. You will remain hands-on while leading architecture decisions, developing reusable ingestion services, and guiding engineers across teams. Your work will support batch, change data capture (CDC), and event-driven ingestion, with clear expectations for data quality, reliability, security, and cost.

WEX is undergoing a data platform transformation—and this team builds the foundation. Every pipeline you create contributes directly to powering analytics, automation, and product intelligence across all business domains.

If you’re passionate about scaling data platforms from the ground up, this is your chance to help shape how WEX ingests and leverages its most valuable asset: data.

What You’ll Do

  • Build and maintain high-performance data acquisition pipelines that integrate with a variety of systems across WEX and third-party vendors.
  • Lead the design and delivery of a modular ingestion platform with reusable connectors and configuration-driven onboarding. Establish metadata and configuration patterns that reduce source-specific development and support Data Acquisition as a Service.
  • Build schema validation, completeness checks, reconciliation, duplicate prevention, and audit logging into shared ingestion components.
  • Support safe retries, replay, backfills, and schema evolution so failures can be recovered without losing or incorrectly duplicating data.
  • Design batch, CDC, and streaming ingestion patterns that meet agreed freshness, throughput, and recovery requirements. Evaluate performance, source-system impact, and operating cost when selecting and extending ingestion technologies.
  • Ensure traceability, lineage, and security through integration with control plane and governance systems.
  • Lead design and code reviews, maintain technical specifications and architectural decisions, and mentor engineers in reusable platform design.
  • Establish automated testing and CI/CD practices for ingestion code, connector configuration, and infrastructure, with validation before production deployment.
  • Partner with the established production support process on complex escalations, root-cause analysis, and preventive engineering improvements.

What You Bring

Required:

  • B.Sc. in Computer Science, Engineering, or related technical field; M.Sc. a plus but not required.
  • 8+ years of software engineering experience, including delivery of production distributed systems or data platforms and demonstrated technical leadership across team boundaries.
  • Strong programming skills in Python, Java, Scala, or another systems-focused language.
  • Experience with data integration and ingestion pipelines—you understand what it means to bring data in from source systems, transform it, and deliver it reliably downstream.
  • Solid grasp of engineering fundamentals, including version control, modular design, testing, and performance tuning.
  • Demonstrated experience designing and operating production integrations that handle schema evolution, failure recovery, observability, and secure access.
  • Ability to lead architecture decisions, explain engineering tradeoffs, resolve dependencies across teams, and guide implementation through production adoption.
  • Practical experience using AI-assisted engineering tools for design, coding, testing, or documentation, with validation of generated outputs for correctness, security, and maintainability.
  • A collaborative mindset—comfortable working across domains, products, and infrastructure layers.
  • A strong sense of ownership and accountability—you care deeply about building systems that last.

Preferred:

  • Experience building reusable connectors, metadata-driven ingestion services, or configuration-driven onboarding capabilities.

What Success Looks Like

During your first year, you will work with engineering and product leadership to establish baselines and agree on outcomes such as:

  • Reducing onboarding lead time and manual effort through shared connectors and configuration-driven patterns.
  • Increasing adoption of reusable ingestion capabilities across sources and teams.
  • Meeting agreed completeness and freshness criteria, with reliable reconciliation and recovery.
  • Improving deployment quality and reducing recurring failures through automated testing and actionable observability.
The base pay range represents the anticipated low and high end of the pay range for this position. Actual pay rates will vary and will be based on various factors, such as your qualifications, skills, competencies, and proficiency for the role. Base pay is one component of WEX's total compensation package. Most sales positions are eligible for commission under the terms of an applicable plan. Non-sales roles are typically eligible for a quarterly or annual bonus based on their role and applicable plan. WEX's comprehensive and market competitive benefits are designed to support your personal and professional well-being. Benefits include health, dental and vision insurances, retirement savings plan, paid time off, health savings account, flexible spending accounts, life insurance, disability insurance, tuition reimbursement, and more. For more information, check out the "About Us" section.Pay Range: $140,600.00 - $173,100.00

jobs.title: Director, Pricing & Monetization
jobs.excerpt: Sprinklr is the definitive, AI-native platform for Unified Customer Experience Management (Unified-CXM), empowering brands to deliver extraordinary experiences at scale — across every customer touchpoint.
jobs.description:
Sprinklr is the definitive, AI-native platform for Unified Customer Experience Management (Unified-CXM), empowering brands to deliver extraordinary experiences at scale — across every customer touchpoint.

By combining human instinct with the speed and efficiency of AI, Sprinklr helps brands earn trust and loyalty through personalized, seamless, and efficient customer interactions. Sprinklr’s unified platform provides powerful solutions for every customer-facing team — spanning social media management, marketing, advertising, customer feedback, and omnichannel contact center management — enabling enterprises to unify data, break down silos, and act on real-time insights.

Today, 1,900+ enterprises and 60% of the Fortune 100 rely on Sprinklr to help them deliver consistent, trusted customer experiences worldwide.

Job Description

The Director, Pricing & Monetization is the enterprise leader accountable for Sprinklr’s pricing, packaging, and monetization strategy. This role sets the multi-year vision and operating model for how the company converts product innovation, customer value, market evidence, and unit economics into scalable commercial offers that customers can understand, sellers can transact, and the company can grow profitably.


The Director will lead a company-wide portfolio of monetization priorities spanning offer architecture, price metrics, packaging tiers, bundles, upgrade paths, consumption and outcome-based models, AI monetization, SKU governance, and commercial rollout. The role serves as a strategic advisor to the VP, Product Operations and executive leadership, and drives decisions across Product, Product Marketing, Finance, Sales, Sales Operations, Deal Desk, Billing, Revenue Accounting, Legal, Customer Success, Services, and Enablement.


This is a remote position with a preference for someone to sit in the Eastern time zone.


What You Will Own

  • Enterprise pricing and packaging strategy. Define the principles, roadmaps, and decision frameworks that guide how Sprinklr packages, prices, sells, and expands its portfolio across Social, Marketing, Insights, Service, Platform, and AI.
  • Offer and portfolio architecture. Create clear package structures, including good-better-best tiers, platform entitlements, add-ons, bundles, buyer-aligned offers, and logical land-expand-unify upgrade paths.
  • Monetization model design. Develop and pressure-test seat, usage, consumption, credit, outcome, and hybrid pricing models; identify the price metric that best aligns customer value, willingness to pay, cost-to-serve, and operational feasibility.
  • Commercial and financial modeling. Build business cases, scenario models, back-tests, migration economics, discount architecture, and sensitivity analyses that quantify ARR, margin, adoption, retention, cannibalization, and revenue-risk implications.
  • Cross-functional pricing decisions. Lead working sessions and executive decision forums; surface trade-offs, recommend a clear path, and drive alignment from concept through approval and launch.
  • Pricing operations and governance. Establish repeatable intake, prioritization, approval, documentation, and lifecycle processes for new offers, SKU creation, migrations, exceptions, deprecations, and pricebook changes.
  • Launch and field readiness. Translate strategy into executable artifacts such as pricebooks, packaging maps, SKU definitions, quoting rules, migration guidance, FAQs, enablement materials, and seller-facing value narratives.
  • Performance management. Define KPIs and learning agendas for new pricing and packaging, monitor adoption and commercial outcomes, and recommend revisions based on evidence from customers, deals, usage, win/loss patterns, and financial results.
  • Market and customer intelligence. Incorporate competitive benchmarks, customer research, buyer personas, willingness-to-pay signals, and product usage into recommendations while distinguishing durable market evidence from one-off deal requests.
  • Multi-year monetization roadmap. Establish a sequenced roadmap across product suites, customer segments, geographies, and channels, balancing transformational priorities with launch commitments, field needs, and operational capacity.
  • Experimentation and optimization. Create a disciplined learning agenda for pricing and offer tests, defining hypotheses, guardrails, success metrics, and decision rules that turn market and customer evidence into continuous improvement.

How You Will Work

  • Bring an independent, evidence-based point of view and recommend decisions rather than only facilitating stakeholder input.
  • Balance strategic coherence with practical speed, distinguishing decisions that require precision from those best advanced through testing and iteration.
  • Build credibility across technical, product, finance, and go-to-market audiences by making complex economics and trade-offs easy to understand.
  • Operate end to end: frame the problem, gather evidence, model alternatives, secure decisions, translate them into systems and field assets, and measure results.
  • Create durable mechanisms, reusable frameworks, and clear documentation so pricing decisions scale beyond a single project or individual.

Required Qualifications

  • 12+ years of progressive experience in B2B technology, enterprise SaaS, pricing, monetization, product strategy, product operations, management consulting, corporate strategy, or a related field, including significant leadership of enterprise pricing and packaging across a complex portfolio.
  • Demonstrated experience designing and launching complex B2B offers across multiple products, buyer groups, deployment models, or geographies.
  • Expertise in pricing architecture, packaging design, value metrics, segmentation, willingness-to-pay research, competitive benchmarking, discounting, and migration strategy.
  • Strong financial and analytical capability, including scenario modeling, unit economics, margin analysis, price-volume-mix thinking, and customer-level back-testing.
  • Experience with recurring-revenue business models: seat-based, usage-based, consumption, credits, outcome-based, transaction, or hybrid pricing.
  • Ability to influence senior Product, Finance, Sales, and executive stakeholders through structured thinking, clear recommendations, and executive-ready communication.
  • Proven record of turning strategy into operational execution across pricebooks, SKUs, quoting workflows, billing requirements, enablement, and performance reporting.
  • Advanced proficiency with Excel or equivalent modeling tools and comfort working with CRM, CPQ, billing, product-usage, and business-intelligence data.
  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience.
  • Demonstrated experience leading a pricing, monetization, commercial strategy, or related team and developing high-performing analytical and strategic talent.
  • Experience presenting material pricing, portfolio, or business-model recommendations to C-suite leaders; board exposure is strongly preferred.
  • Proven ability to establish enterprise governance, prioritize a portfolio of competing monetization initiatives, and drive adoption across a global matrixed organization.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in enterprise SaaS, customer experience management, contact center, marketing technology, social media management, analytics, or AI software.
  • Experience monetizing AI, automation, data, API, platform, or agentic capabilities using credits, consumption, outcomes, or blended commercial models.
  • Familiarity with Salesforce and enterprise CPQ/pricebook processes, product telemetry, revenue-recognition considerations, and usage-based billing operations.
  • Experience partnering with external pricing advisors or applying methodologies such as conjoint analysis, Van Westendorp, Gabor-Granger, value-driver segmentation, and price-volume sensitivity analysis.
  • MBA or advanced degree in business, economics, finance, analytics, or a related field.

We focus on our mission: Sprinklr was founded in 2009 to solve a big problem: growing enterprise complexity that separated brands from their customers. Our vision was clear: to unify fragmented teams, tools and data — helping large organizations build deeper, more meaningful connections with the people they serve. Today, Sprinklr has a unified, AI-native platform for four product suites: Sprinklr Service, Sprinklr Social, Sprinklr Marketing, and Sprinklr Insights. Sprinklr is here to do three things:

  • Lead a new category of enterprise software that we call Unified-CXM.

  • Empower companies to deliver next generation, unified engagement journeys that reimagine the customer experience.

  • Create a culture of customer obsession, with trust, teamwork, and accountability.

We believe in our product: Customers who value exceptional customer experiences have what they need on our single unified platform, built with an operating system approach on a single codebase. That means that everything — and everyone — can work together to service, respond, sell, and market to customers on the channels they prefer. While Unified Customer Experience Management (Unified-CXM) as a category is just getting started, we are well on our way to creating a no-compromise, unified approach to better customer experiences for the world’s leading enterprise brands.

We invest in our people: We offer a comprehensive suite of benefits designed to help each member of our team thrive. Sprinklr believes that you should be able to get the type of care you need for your personal well-being when you need it. Our open Mentoring Program is designed to create meaningful connections that support growth and amplify our focus.

Reasonable accommodations are available upon request during the interview process. To request an accommodation, please work directly with your recruitment coordinator or recruiter.

JOB REQ COMPENSATION RANGE

$146,000 - $244,000

The base salary range for this role is shown above. At Sprinklr, base pay depends on multiple individualized factors, including experience, qualifications, job-related knowledge and skills, and geographic location. US-based Sprinklr employees are eligible for a highly competitive benefits package as well, which demonstrates our commitment to our employees’ health, well-being, and financial protection. What success looks like in this role:

Position Overview 

  • The Delivery Manager is responsible for leading managed infrastructure and workload automation services across multiple technology disciplines. This role provides operational leadership for Workload Automation and the Incident Response Team (IRT), a first-level Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) function responsible for monitoring, triage, incident response, technical coordination and service restoration across supported environments. 
  • The role requires a strong working knowledge of enterprise infrastructure and workload automation technologies, including Control-M, AutoSys, Tivoli and other applicable workload automation platforms, Windows, Linux, backup and restore, storage, databases, and cloud platforms such as OCI, AWS and Microsoft Azure. The individual must be able to effectively lead technical teams, manage operational risks and escalations, and communicate technical issues and business impact to clients and stakeholders. 
  • Automation is a core component of this role. The successful candidate should have demonstrated experience identifying opportunities to automate repeatable operational activities, reduce manual intervention, improve reliability and drive measurable improvements in service delivery. 
  • The ideal candidate should enjoy working in a fast-paced and dynamic environment, exercise sound business judgment, and apply strong problem-solving and collaboration skills across a complex organization. 
  • Recruit, develop, inspire and retain a high-performing operations and engineering team while promoting accountability, knowledge sharing and continuous improvement. 

Business and Industry Skills 

  • Demonstrates working knowledge across infrastructure operations, workload automation, SRE practices and managed services delivery. Stays current with relevant IT infrastructure, cloud, automation and service-management technologies, ITIL practices and vendor offerings. 
  • Communicates in an open, candid, clear, complete and consistent manner. Listens well, conveys technical and business information in easily understood formats, and demonstrates professionalism in formal and informal interactions. 
  • Understands the meaning and implications of key operational and financial indicators and uses data to identify issues, evaluate service performance and develop practical improvement plans. 
  • Collaborates effectively across technology towers, client teams, account leadership, engineering teams and third-party suppliers to drive service outcomes. 

Responsibilities 

Managed Service Delivery 

  • Manage day-to-day delivery of infrastructure, workload automation and Incident Response Team services. 
  • Ensure achievement of SLA, KPI, availability, quality and operational performance objectives. 
  • Provide leadership during service-impacting incidents and escalations, ensuring the appropriate technical resources and stakeholders are engaged. 
  • Drive operational accountability across technology teams and ensure issues are followed through to resolution. 
  • Identify recurring operational issues and partner with engineering teams to implement permanent corrective actions. 
  • Maintain appropriate staffing, skills, coverage, documentation and operational readiness across supported services. 
  • Manage relationships with clients, internal stakeholders, technology partners and third-party suppliers. 
  • Validate that staffing levels, skill levels and other resources align with contractual, financial and solution requirements. 
  • Identify resource or capability gaps and document associated risks, mitigation plans and contingencies. 

Incident Response / SRE Operations 

  • Provide leadership for the Incident Response Team, supporting first and second-level SRE and infrastructure operations. 
  • Ensure effective monitoring, event management, incident triage, escalation, troubleshooting and service-restoration processes. 
  • Coordinate support across Windows, Linux, backup and restore, storage, database, cloud and other infrastructure technologies. 
  • Promote proactive operations by identifying repeat incidents, alert noise, manual activities and opportunities for improved monitoring and automation. 
  • Partner with engineering and technology tower teams for complex incidents, problem management, root-cause analysis and continuous improvement. 

Workload Automation 

  • Provide service delivery leadership for enterprise workload automation and job-scheduling platforms, including Control-M, AutoSys, Tivoli and other applicable workload automation technologies. 
  • Apply a working understanding of workload scheduling concepts, dependencies, job failures, batch processing, alerting, escalation and operational recovery. 
  • Ensure workload automation incidents and failures are appropriately prioritized, investigated, escalated and communicated. 
  • Work with technical teams to improve workload reliability and reduce repetitive manual intervention. 
  • Support continuous improvement of workload automation processes, monitoring, support procedures and operational controls. 

Automation and Continuous Improvement 

  • Champion an automation-first approach to operational service delivery. 
  • Identify repetitive support activities, manual processes and recurring incidents that are candidates for automation. 
  • Partner with engineering teams to develop and implement automation that reduces manual effort, improves service reliability and accelerates incident resolution. 
  • Apply a working understanding of common infrastructure automation, scripting, orchestration and Infrastructure as Code concepts. 
  • Track the operational benefits of automation initiatives and continuously identify additional opportunities for improvement. 
  • Promote standardization, documentation, knowledge management and reusable operational processes across teams. 

Service Governance and Commercial Support 

  • Review service performance, risks, resource needs and improvement opportunities with account and client stakeholders. 
  • Support account management and bid teams by reviewing relevant service-delivery requirements, staffing assumptions, operational risks and solution dependencies when requested. 
  • Participate in governance and service-review activities to maintain a shared understanding of operational expectations, performance and priorities. 


You will be successful in this role if you have:

Skills, Experience & Qualifications 

  • Progressive experience in IT infrastructure operations, managed services, service delivery, SRE, workload automation or enterprise operations. 
  • Previous experience leading multidisciplinary technical or operations teams. 
  • Demonstrated experience managing services in environments involving Windows, Linux, storage, backup and recovery, database and cloud technologies. 
  • BA/BS degree and 5+ years’ relevant experience OR equivalent combination of education and relevant experience 2 years’ leadership experience

Preferred Skills:

SailPoint Engineering Lead, IAM

Location: Dallas, TX | Ashburn, VA | Denver, CO | Charlotte, NC | Boston, MA | New York, NY | Austin, TX ,and open for (Remote)

Your Role

You will serve as the internal owner and technical authority for Digital Realty's SailPoint Identity Security Cloud (ISC) platform, defining how identity governance operates at enterprise scale. This role leads the Identity Governance and Administration (IGA) strategy, architecture, and delivery, ensuring access lifecycle management, certifications, and compliance controls are designed and executed to meet global regulatory and operational requirements. As the enterprise lead for SailPoint ISC, you will drive the evolution of Digital Realty's identity governance program while partnering across Security, Infrastructure, Compliance, and Business teams. This is not an execution role—it is a program leadership position with direct accountability for how identity governance operates across a globally regulated enterprise.

What You'll Do

  • Own and drive the multi-year IGA roadmap and strategy.
  • Define SailPoint ISC architecture across Joiner-Mover-Leaver (JML) lifecycle processes, access certifications, role models, and connectors.
  • Design integrations with Oracle HCM, Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID, ServiceNow, BeyondTrust, and Microsoft Sentinel.
  • Build and deliver SailPoint ISC capabilities, including workflows, lifecycle rules, access requests, and certification campaigns.
  • Establish configuration-as-code practices utilizing GitHub, CI/CD pipelines, source control, and automated testing as the standard operating model.
  • Lead, mentor, and quality-gate offshore delivery teams.
  • Govern systems integrator (SI) partners and ensure deliverables meet architecture, security, and operational standards.
  • Own SOX User Access Review (UAR) campaigns, audit evidence collection, and compliance engagements.
  • Ensure identity governance controls align with regulatory requirements, including NIS2 and DORA.
  • Define and implement governance for non-human identities, including service accounts, APIs, machine identities, and privileged access integrations.

What You'll Need

  • 8–10 years of Identity and Access Management (IAM) experience, including 4+ years of hands-on SailPoint Identity Security Cloud (IdentityNow) experience.
  • Proven experience designing and implementing end-to-end Joiner-Mover-Leaver (JML) lifecycle processes.
  • Experience owning enterprise IGA architecture and delivering multi-year roadmap initiatives.
  • Strong expertise in access certifications, SOX User Access Reviews (UARs), audit readiness, and compliance engagement.
  • Deep knowledge of non-human identity governance, including service account lifecycle management, NHI discovery and classification, PAM/IGA integration, and secrets management practices.
  • Experience operating identity governance programs within large-scale enterprise environments supporting 10,000+ identities.
  • DevOps mindset with hands-on experience implementing CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, and configuration-as-code methodologies.
  • Advanced SailPoint ISC technical expertise, including rules, APIs, connectors, workflows, and integrations.
  • Experience integrating identity platforms with Oracle HCM, Active Directory, and Microsoft Entra ID.
  • SailPoint ISC Certified Engineer (or equivalent) strongly preferred; CISSP and/or CISM certifications preferred.

A Bit About Us

Digital Realty brings companies and data together by delivering the full spectrum of data center, colocation and interconnection solutions. PlatformDIGITAL®, the company's global data center platform, provides customers with a secure data meeting place and a proven Pervasive Datacenter Architecture (PDx®) solution methodology for powering innovation and efficiently managing Data Gravity challenges. Digital Realty gives its customers access to the connected data communities that matter to them with a global data center footprint of 300+ facilities in 50+ metros across 25+ countries on six continents.

To learn more about Digital Realty, please visit digitalrealty.com or follow us on LinkedIn and Twitter.

A Bit About Our Team

Technology & Innovation

Our Technology & Innovation team strives to innovate alongside our customers and empower their businesses to thrive. We work closely with our customers to develop insights-based, data-driven technical solutions and differentiated value propositions on PlatformDIGITAL® across the world. Operating in almost 50 cities globally means we understand how rapidly the world is evolving, so we've built a best-in-class development model to qualify, package, and enable cloud-to-core-to-edge hybrid IT solutions. Our deep technical heritage, combined with our global footprint, allows us to create and deploy services and solutions that are at the heart of the digital economy.

What We Can Offer You

Our rapidly evolving business sector offers the opportunity to be part of a courageous and passionate team who work together to understand and meet the changing needs of our global customers.

Join us and you'll be part of a supportive and inclusive environment where you can bring your whole self to work. As part of our team, you'll get to work with people from different business areas, challenge the way we do things and put your ideas into action. We'll also give you plenty of development opportunities so you can build a rewarding and successful career with us.

Apply today, take charge of your career and grow your talents with us.

Health and Safety

Safety isn't just a priority here at Digital Realty; it's critical to everything we do. Safeguarding lives, protecting assets, and securing data aren't just ideals—they're essential pillars of our commitment to excellence for our people, our partners, and our customers. We have a culture of care where every member of Team Digital embraces a relentless pursuit of working safely across Digital Realty. Together we are Safely Powering Progress.

Our Compensation Philosophy

Digital Realty offers its employees a highly competitive compensation package, excellent benefits, and an environment that recognizes and rewards your contributions. Central to our compensation philosophy is rewarding our employees for achieving the values and objectives aligned to the company's overall goals and values.

$140,000 - $180,000 USD annually
